13 Appendix: Time-reversal and separable pseudopotential in EPW

Building on the derivation proposed in Ref. [46], we extend the equations to treat the particular case of crystals with no inversion symmetry. In these cases, it is possible to take advantage of time-reversal symmetry to decrease the number of irreducible 𝐪\mathbf{q}-points required on the coarse grid.

Within linear response, the change of the self-consistent potential with respect to a collective ionic displacement Δ​𝝉κ​p𝐪​ν\Delta\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\kappa p}^{\mathbf{q}\nu} with phonon momentum 𝐪\mathbf{q} and mode index ν\nu can be obtained from the screening of the bare ionic potential Vκion​(𝐫)V^{\text{ion}}_{\kappa}(\mathbf{r}) as:

∂𝐪​νV⁡(𝐫)=∂∂η​∫d​𝐫′​ε−1​(𝐫,𝐫′)​∑κ,𝐑pVκion​(𝐫′−𝝉κ​p−η​Δ​𝝉κ​p𝐪​ν),\partial_{\mathbf{q}\nu}V(\mathbf{r})=\\ \frac{\partial}{\partial\eta}\int d\mathbf{r}^{\prime}\varepsilon^{-1}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r^{\prime}})\sum_{\kappa,\mathbf{R}_{p}}V^{\text{ion}}_{\kappa}(\mathbf{r}^{\prime}-\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\kappa p}-\eta\Delta\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\kappa p}^{\mathbf{q}\nu}), (63)

where ε−1​(𝐫,𝐫′)\varepsilon^{-1}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r^{\prime}}) is the electronic dielectric function and 𝝉κ​p\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\kappa p} is the coordinate of each ion κ\kappa in the unit cell centered at 𝐑p\mathbf{R}_{p}.

The ionic displacement can be expressed in the basis of the periodic and normalized vibrational eigenmodes 𝐞𝐪​κν\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{q}\kappa}^{\nu}:

Δ​𝝉κ​p𝐪​ν=m0mκ​𝐞𝐪​κν​ei​𝐪⋅𝐑p,\Delta\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\kappa p}^{\mathbf{q}\nu}=\sqrt{\frac{m_{0}}{m_{\kappa}}}\mathbf{e}_{\mathbf{q}\kappa}^{\nu}e^{i\mathbf{q}\cdot\mathbf{R}_{p}}, (64)

where mκm_{\kappa} is the ionic mass of atom κ\kappa.

Following the convention defined in Ref. [179], the application of a symmetry operation {𝒮|𝐯}\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\} on a real space point 𝐫\mathbf{r} gives {𝒮|𝐯}​𝐫=𝒮​𝐫+𝐯\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r}=\mathcal{S}\mathbf{r}+\mathbf{v}, with 𝒮\mathcal{S} the rotation part and 𝐯\mathbf{v} the possible fractional translation.

Considering that the symmetry operation {𝒮|𝐯}\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\} maps κ​p\kappa p into κ′​p′\kappa^{\prime}p^{\prime}, that the dielectric function is invariant under {𝒮|𝐯}\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}, and that the ionic part of the pseudopotential is invariant under 𝒮\mathcal{S}, we obtain:

∂𝒮​𝐪​νV⁡(𝐫)=∂𝐪​νV⁡({𝒮|𝐯}−1​𝐫).\partial_{\mathcal{S}\mathbf{q}\nu}V(\mathbf{r})=\partial_{\mathbf{q}\nu}V(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}^{-1}\mathbf{r}). (65)

The electron-phonon matrix element introduced in Eq. (2) for momentum transfer 𝒮​𝐪\mathcal{S}\mathbf{q} then reads:

gm​n,ν​(𝐤,𝒮​𝐪)=12​ω𝒮​𝐪​ν​⟨ψm​𝐤+𝒮​𝐪​(𝐫)|∂𝐪​νV⁡({𝒮|𝐯}−1​𝐫)|(𝐫)​ψn​𝐤⟩,g_{mn,\nu}(\mathbf{k,\mathcal{S}q})=\\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\omega_{\mathcal{S}\mathbf{q}\nu}}}\big\langle\psi_{m\mathbf{k+\mathcal{S}q}}(\mathbf{r})\big|\partial_{\mathbf{q}\nu}V(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}^{-1}\mathbf{r})\big|(\mathbf{r})\psi_{n\mathbf{k}}\big\rangle, (66)

which, after a change of spatial variable and noting that ω𝒮​𝐪​ν=ω𝐪​ν\omega_{\mathcal{S}\mathbf{q}\nu}=\omega_{\mathbf{q}\nu}, becomes:

gm​n,ν​(𝐤,𝒮​𝐪)=12​ω𝐪​ν​⟨ψm​𝐤+𝒮​𝐪​({𝒮|𝐯}​𝐫)|∂𝐪​νV⁡(𝐫)|ψn​𝐤​({𝒮|𝐯}​𝐫)⟩.g_{mn,\nu}(\mathbf{k,\mathcal{S}q})=\\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\omega_{\mathbf{q}\nu}}}\big\langle\psi_{m\mathbf{k+\mathcal{S}q}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\partial_{\mathbf{q}\nu}V(\mathbf{r})\big|\psi_{n\mathbf{k}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle. (67)

To simplify the above equation, in principle one could use the following relationship:

ψm​𝐤+𝒮​𝐪​({𝒮|𝐯}​𝐫)=ψm​𝒮−𝟏​𝐤+𝐪​(𝐫).\psi_{m\mathbf{k+\mathcal{S}q}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})=\psi_{m\mathbf{\mathcal{S}^{-1}k+q}}(\mathbf{r}). (68)

However, such equality implies a phase relationship which is not enforced in electronic structure codes, and therefore does not hold in general.

In case of a separable pseudopotential based on the Kleinman and Bylander (KB) procedure [180], by using the completeness of the planewaves basis ∑𝐆|𝐤+𝐆⟩​⟨𝐤+𝐆|=1\sum_{\mathbf{G}}|\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}\rangle\langle\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}|=1, Eq. (67) becomes:

gm​n,ν​(𝐤,𝒮​𝐪)=12​ω𝐪​ν[⟨ψm​𝐤+𝒮​𝐪({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)|∂𝐪​νVscf(𝐫)|ψn​𝐤({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)⟩+∑𝐆𝐆′⟨ψm​𝐤+𝒮​𝐪({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)|𝐤+𝒮𝐪+𝐆({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)⟩×⟨𝐤+𝒮​𝐪+𝐆⁡({𝒮|𝐯}​𝐫)|∂𝐪​νVion​(𝐫)|𝐤+𝐆′​({𝒮|𝐯}​𝐫)⟩×⟨𝐤+𝐆′({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)|ψn​𝐤({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)⟩],g_{mn,\nu}(\mathbf{k,\mathcal{S}q})=\\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\omega_{\mathbf{q}\nu}}}\Big[\big\langle\psi_{m\mathbf{k+\mathcal{S}q}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\partial_{\mathbf{q}\nu}V^{\text{scf}}(\mathbf{r})\big|\psi_{n\mathbf{k}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\\ +\sum_{\mathbf{G}\mathbf{G^{\prime}}}\big\langle\psi_{m\mathbf{k+\mathcal{S}q}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\mathbf{k}+\mathcal{S}\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{G}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\\ \times\big\langle\mathbf{k}+\mathcal{S}\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{G}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\partial_{\mathbf{q}\nu}V^{\text{ion}}(\mathbf{r})\big|\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}^{\prime}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\\ \times\big\langle\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}^{\prime}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\psi_{n\mathbf{k}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\Big], (69)

where Vscf​(𝐫)V^{\text{scf}}(\mathbf{r}) is the screening contribution (local in DFT) that is computed in real space for convenience and then Fourier transformed back. Since the ionic part of the potential VionV^{\text{ion}} needs to be computed at 𝐫\mathbf{r} we have introduced a complete plane wave basis set. The basis functions |𝐤+𝐆⟩|\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}\rangle respect the relationship given in Eq. (68) and therefore we can deduce:

gm​n,ν​(𝐤,𝒮​𝐪)=12​ω𝐪​ν[⟨ψm​𝐤+𝒮​𝐪({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)|∂𝐪​νVscf(𝐫)|ψn​𝐤({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)⟩+∑𝐆𝐆′⟨ψm​𝐤+𝒮​𝐪({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)|𝐤+𝒮𝐪+𝐆({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)⟩×⟨𝒮−1​𝐤+𝐪+𝐆⁡(𝐫)|∂𝐪​νVion​(𝐫)|𝒮−1​𝐤+𝐆′​(𝐫)⟩×⟨𝐤+𝐆′({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)|ψn​𝐤({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)⟩].g_{mn,\nu}(\mathbf{k,\mathcal{S}q})=\\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\omega_{\mathbf{q}\nu}}}\Big[\big\langle\psi_{m\mathbf{k+\mathcal{S}q}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\partial_{\mathbf{q}\nu}V^{\text{scf}}(\mathbf{r})\big|\psi_{n\mathbf{k}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\\ +\sum_{\mathbf{G}\mathbf{G^{\prime}}}\big\langle\psi_{m\mathbf{k+\mathcal{S}q}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\mathbf{k}+\mathcal{S}\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{G}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\\ \times\big\langle\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{G}(\mathbf{r})\big|\partial_{\mathbf{q}\nu}V^{\text{ion}}(\mathbf{r})\big|\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}^{\prime}(\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\\ \times\big\langle\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}^{\prime}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\psi_{n\mathbf{k}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\Big]. (70)

The second term can be expressed in reciprocal space as follows, see Eq. (A14) of Ref. [45]:

⟨𝒮−1​𝐤+𝐪+𝐆|∂𝐪​νVion|𝒮−1​𝐤+𝐆′⟩=∑κ−i(qν+Gν−Gν′)e−i(𝐪+𝐆−𝐆′)⋅𝝉κ[v~κloc(𝐪+𝐆−𝐆′)+∑l∑m=−llv~κ,l​m(𝒮−1𝐤+𝐪+𝐆,𝒮−1𝐤+𝐆′)].\big\langle\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{G}\big|\partial_{\mathbf{q}\nu}V^{\text{ion}}\big|\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}^{\prime}\big\rangle=\\ \sum_{\kappa}-i\big(q_{\nu}+G_{\nu}-G_{\nu}^{\prime})e^{-i(\mathbf{q+G-G^{\prime}})\cdot\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\kappa}}\bigg[\tilde{v}_{\kappa}^{\text{loc}}(\mathbf{q+G-G^{\prime}})\\ +\sum_{l}\sum_{m=-l}^{l}\tilde{v}_{\kappa,lm}(\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{G},\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}^{\prime})\bigg]. (71)

Here the exponential is the structure factor, v~κloc\tilde{v}_{\kappa}^{\text{loc}} is the Fourier transform of the local part of the pseudopotential, and v~κ,l​m\tilde{v}_{\kappa,lm} is the non-local part defined as:

v~κ,l​m​(𝒮−1​𝐤+𝐪+𝐆,𝒮−1​𝐤+𝐆′)=cκ,l​m​β~κ,l​m∗​(𝒮−1​𝐤+𝐪+𝐆)​β~κ,l​m​(𝒮−1​𝐤+𝐆′),\tilde{v}_{\kappa,lm}(\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{G},\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}^{\prime})=\\ c_{\kappa,lm}\,\tilde{\beta}_{\kappa,lm}^{*}(\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{G})\,\tilde{\beta}_{\kappa,lm}(\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}^{\prime}), (72)

where β~κ,l​m\tilde{\beta}_{\kappa,lm} is the Fourier transform of the KB projectors:

βκ,l​m​(𝐫)=V^κ​l​(r)​ϕl​mps​(𝐫),\beta_{\kappa,lm}(\mathbf{r})=\hat{V}_{\kappa l}(r)\phi_{lm}^{\text{ps}}(\mathbf{r}), (73)

and the coefficient cκ,l​mc_{\kappa,lm} are given by:

cκ,l​m=1⟨ϕl​mps​(𝐫)|V^κ​l​(r)|ϕl​mps​(𝐫)⟩.c_{\kappa,lm}=\frac{1}{\big\langle\phi_{lm}^{\text{ps}}(\mathbf{r})\big|\hat{V}_{\kappa l}(r)\big|\phi_{lm}^{\text{ps}}(\mathbf{r})\big\rangle}. (74)

In these expression ϕl​mps​(𝐫)\phi_{lm}^{\text{ps}}(\mathbf{r}) is the atomic pseudo-wavefunction, and V^κ​l​(r)\hat{V}_{\kappa l}(r) is the angular momentum component of the pseudopotential.

Having expressed the rotated matrix element in the KB form, we can write the time-reversed version of Eq. (70) that we implemented in the code:

gm​n,ν​(𝐤,−𝒮​𝐪)=12​ω𝐪​ν[⟨ψm​𝐤−𝒮​𝐪({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)|(∂𝐪​νVscf(𝐫))∗|ψn​𝐤({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)⟩+∑𝐆𝐆′⟨ψm​𝐤−𝒮​𝐪({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)|𝐤−𝒮𝐪+𝐆({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)⟩×⟨𝒮−1​𝐤−𝐪+𝐆⁡(𝐫)|∂−𝐪​νVion​(𝐫)|𝒮−1​𝐤+𝐆′​(𝐫)⟩×⟨𝐤+𝐆′({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)|ψn​𝐤({𝒮|𝐯}𝐫)⟩].g_{mn,\nu}(\mathbf{k,-\mathcal{S}q})=\\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\omega_{\mathbf{q}\nu}}}\Big[\big\langle\psi_{m\mathbf{k-\mathcal{S}q}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\Big(\partial_{\mathbf{q}\nu}V^{\text{scf}}(\mathbf{r})\Big)^{*}\big|\psi_{n\mathbf{k}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\\ +\sum_{\mathbf{G}\mathbf{G^{\prime}}}\big\langle\psi_{m\mathbf{k-\mathcal{S}q}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\mathbf{k}-\mathcal{S}\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{G}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\\ \times\big\langle\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}-\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{G}(\mathbf{r})\big|\partial_{-\mathbf{q}\nu}V^{\text{ion}}(\mathbf{r})\big|\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}^{\prime}(\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\\ \times\big\langle\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}^{\prime}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big|\psi_{n\mathbf{k}}(\{\mathcal{S}|\mathbf{v}\}\mathbf{r})\big\rangle\Big]. (75)

14 Appendix: Specific heat in MgB2 and the two-gap BCS model

By free energy minimization, Bardeen, Cooper and Schrieffer obtained an integro-differential equation that links the inverse of the interaction strength λ\lambda to the superconducting gap Δ⁡(T=0)\Delta(T=0) (see Eq. (3.27) of Ref. [77]):

1λ\displaystyle\frac{1}{\lambda} =1N⁡(εF)​ΩBZ\displaystyle=\frac{1}{N(\varepsilon_{F})\Omega_{\text{BZ}}}
=∫0ℏ​ωd​ξ​tanh⁡[12​kB​T​[ξ2+Δ2​(T)]1/2][ξ2+Δ2​(T)]1/2,\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{\hbar\omega}d\xi\frac{\tanh\Big[\frac{1}{2k_{B}T}[\xi^{2}+\Delta^{2}(T)]^{1/2}\Big]}{[\xi^{2}+\Delta^{2}(T)]^{1/2}}, (76)

where λ\lambda is the isotropic integrated λ𝐪​ν\lambda_{\mathbf{q}\nu} from Eq. (11). Here ℏ\hbar and kBk_{B} are indicated explicitly to be consistent with the seminal equation in Ref. [77].

They also derived what is now known as the universal BCS relation for weak coupling (i.e. ℏ​ω≫Δ⁡(T=0)\hbar\omega\gg\Delta(T=0)), see Eq. (3.30) of Ref. [77]:

Δ⁡(T=0)=1.75​kB​Tc.\Delta(T=0)=1.75k_{B}T_{c}. (77)

Finally, using a variational approximation to the true ground-state, they deduced (see Eq. (2.40) of Ref. [77]):

ℏ​ωΔ⁡(T=0)=sinh⁡[1λ].\frac{\hbar\omega}{\Delta(T=0)}=\sinh\Big[\frac{1}{\lambda}\Big]. (78)

We can also define the following two dimensionless variables:

δ=Δ⁡(T)Δ⁡(T=0) and ​τ=TTc.\delta=\frac{\Delta(T)}{\Delta(T=0)}\quad\text{ and }\tau=\frac{T}{T_{c}}. (79)

Inserting Eqs. (77) and (78) inside Eq. (76) and performing a change of variable z=ξΔ⁡(T)z=\frac{\xi}{\Delta(T)} leads to [177]

1λ=∫0δ−1​sinh⁡(1/λ)d​z(1+z2)1/2​tanh⁡[1.752​δτ​(1+z2)1/2].\frac{1}{\lambda}=\int_{0}^{\delta^{-1}\sinh(1/\lambda)}\frac{dz}{(1+z^{2})^{1/2}}\tanh\Big[\frac{1.75}{2}\frac{\delta}{\tau}(1+z^{2})^{1/2}\Big]. (80)

In the case of MgB2, λ=0.75\lambda=0.75 and therefore Eq. (80) can be solved by fixing τ\tau and solving for δ\delta. However, Eq. (80) is expected to work for weak coupling superconductors in the range of λ≤0.3\lambda\leq 0.3 (determined empirically, see Ref. [178], p.112 for more details). Indeed, as can be seen on Fig. 23, the equation has no solution for τ\tau close to 1.

An alternative fitting formula can be used [90]:

Δ⁡(T)Δ⁡(T=0)=1−τp,\frac{\Delta(T)}{\Delta(T=0)}=\sqrt{1-\tau^{p}}, (81)

where pp has to be fitted. By fitting on the solution of Eq. (80) in the low τ\tau value range, we found p=3.3p=3.3 (see Fig. (23)) for λ=0.75\lambda=0.75.

Once we have a value for the isotropic superconducting gap Δ⁡(T)\Delta(T), Eqs. (44) and (46) can be simplified to:

ΔF=−πT∑j[ωj2+Δ2​(T)−ωj]×[Zj−ZjN​ωjωj2+Δ2​(T)],\Delta F=-\pi T\sum_{j}\Big[\sqrt{\omega_{j}^{2}+\Delta^{2}(T)}-\omega_{j}\Big]\\ \times\Big[Z_{j}-Z_{j}^{N}\frac{\omega_{j}}{\sqrt{\omega_{j}^{2}+\Delta^{2}(T)}}\Big], (82)

with

Zj=1+π​Tωj​∑j′ωj′ωj′2+Δ2​(T)​λZ_{j}=1+\frac{\pi T}{\omega_{j}}\sum_{j^{\prime}}\frac{\omega_{j^{\prime}}}{\sqrt{\omega_{j^{\prime}}^{2}+\Delta^{2}(T)}}\lambda (83)

and

ZjN=1+π​Tωj​λ,Z_{j}^{N}=1+\frac{\pi T}{\omega_{j}}\lambda, (84)

where the sum over jj and j′j^{\prime} has to be numerically truncated so that

ωj=(2​j+1)​π​T≤ωc.\omega_{j}=(2j+1)\pi T\leq\omega_{c}. (85)

In our case we used a truncation energy of ωc=0.3\omega_{c}=0.3 eV.
